title: Mercy, Not Sacrifice
question: Why would God prefer mercy to the offerings He Himself commanded?
blurb: A line Jesus quoted twice. See what the prophets and the Gospels do with it.

nodes.content: Why would God prefer mercy to the offerings He Himself commanded?

nodes.verseText: For I desire mercy, not sacrifice, and the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy, not sacrifice.’ For I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners.”

But Samuel declared: “Does the LORD delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as much as in obedience to His voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness is better than the fat of rams.
Learn to do right; seek justice and correct the oppressor. Defend the fatherless and plead the case of the widow.”

For You do not delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; You take no pleasure in burnt offerings. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, You will not despise.
